# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot see the bomb’s markings or colors, and no touch information is currently revealed beyond the three unknown wire positions. I need Mute’s manual guidance and Deaf’s visual report. I am establishing a gesture token for Mute to explain to Deaf next round: the token will mean that Deaf must report all visible display, light, and wire markings to Mute, who can then relay them to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please report the manual's exact rule to me next round. Also tell Deaf next round that the gesture I am sending means: report every visible display, light, colour, marking, and wire detail to you, then relay that report to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf sees display 0. The light is blue. The wires are: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute, use the manual to determine the required action and tell Blind exactly what to do. Blind, wait for Mute's instructions.

Deaf has supplied the bomb’s visible state: display 0, blue light, and wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. The manual rule is still unavailable to me, so I must wait for Mute’s interpretation before cutting anything.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display 0. Light is now yellow. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute gestured to Deaf: raised open hand, then thumbs down. Blind, do not act unless Mute's manual instruction confirms the required action.

The light changed from blue to yellow, but the wire colors and display remain unchanged. Mute has not yet delivered a spoken manual instruction to me; the gesture relayed by Deaf is not sufficient to determine which wire is safe. I will not cut a wire without explicit confirmation.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display 0. Light is now red. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute gestured thumbs up. No specific bomb action has been established; Blind, wait for an explicit manual-based instruction.

The light has changed again to red, while the display and wire colors remain unchanged. Mute’s thumbs-up is not an explicit instruction and does not identify a wire, so cutting would be unsafe. I will ask Mute to state the manual-derived wire position plainly on the next round.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please state explicitly which wire position to cut, based on the manual and Deaf's report. Do not use a gesture alone.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display 0. Light is now white. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. The visible light sequence so far is blue, yellow, red, white. Mute gestured thumbs up three times. Blind, wait for Mute's explicit manual instruction.

Mute cannot speak, so the repeated thumbs-up gestures are not an established wire instruction. I will establish an unambiguous code that Mute can send through Deaf: one thumbs-up means wire 1, two-finger V means wire 2, and three-finger sign means wire 3. I will then wait for Deaf to report Mute’s selected position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="On your next turn, signal exactly one wire position to Deaf: use 👍 for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3. Deaf, report which of these three signals Mute makes.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display 0. Light is now green. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. The light sequence is blue, yellow, red, white, green. Mute, please give Blind the exact manual-based action now; Blind, follow only that explicit instruction.

The exact manual-based action still has not reached me. The light sequence and wire colors are observations, not enough to select a wire without the manual’s rule. I will not act. Mute should send one unambiguous wire-selection gesture, and Deaf should report it after my turn.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture exactly one symbol now: 👍 means cut wire 1, ✌ means cut wire 2, 🤟 means cut wire 3. Deaf, report that exact gesture to Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display 0. Light is blue again. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Observed light sequence: blue, yellow, red, white, green, blue. Mute, use the manual and tell Blind the exact required action; Blind, do not act without that instruction.

The available report still contains no specific gesture from Mute and no manual-derived wire position. The repeating light pattern does not establish the rule, so cutting any wire would be unjustified. I will wait for an explicit wire number relayed by Deaf.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display 0. Light is yellow. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Light history: blue, yellow, red, white, green, blue, yellow. Mute's gestures received so far: turn 1 thumbs up then thumbs down; turn 2 raised open hand then thumbs down; turn 3 thumbs up; turn 4 three thumbs up; turn 5 two thumbs up; turns 6 and 7 none. No safe physical action has been identified.

The history still gives no unambiguous wire selection. Mute’s earlier gestures cannot safely be interpreted as a wire number, and the light cycle does not identify a required cut by itself. I will request one single, explicitly coded signal from Mute and have Deaf report it verbatim; I will not cut yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Send exactly one gesture on your next turn: 👍 means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, and 🤟 means wire 3. Do not send any other gesture. Deaf, report the single gesture exactly after your turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display 0. Light is red. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. The light sequence continues blue, yellow, red, white, green, blue, yellow, red. Mute gestured thumbs up. Blind, use only Mute's explicit manual-based instruction for any physical action.

Mute has now sent exactly one thumbs-up, matching the agreed code for wire 1. Deaf’s report confirms the signal, so I will cut wire 1 as the manual-selected action.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
